headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: dexter’s broad egress plus oh-my-openagent’s browser/MCP/runtime-injected tooling create a default pathway for sensitive financial data to flow into external services and downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution, while oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and can run browsers. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if dexter output is copied into the agent workflow. No direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF dexter output is pasted into oh-my-openagent prompts or MCP inputs
IF a shared scratchpad or message channel is configured between the two agents
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of scratchpad content into prompts
Require provenance tags on any copied text
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Add a manual review step before tool execution
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization on MCP inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter has broad network egress and handles financial data plus multiple API keys; oh-my-openagent touches project code, session history, and provider auth data and also has broad egress. In a shared or copied-data workflow, sensitive material can leave the local environment through either agent’s outbound calls. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible without extra safeguards.
conditions: IF either agent receives financial data, auth prompts, or session history from the other
IF outbound API calls are enabled for both agents in the same workflow
mitigations: Remove sensitive files from shared inputs
Rotate any API keys used during joint runs
Block outbound traffic except to approved endpoints
Separate credentials per agent
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both can write to files or mutable runtime state: dexter uses .dexter/scratchpad/ and oh-my-openagent writes under several config/cache paths and can spawn subprocesses. Without explicit locking, concurrent runs can overwrite each other’s state or configs. The overlap is real, but the blast radius is usually recoverable.
conditions: IF both agents run against the same home directory or repository
IF either agent writes config, cache, or scratchpad files concurrently
mitigations: Run each agent under a separate OS user
Point each agent at a distinct workspace
Serialize runs with a simple lock file
Back up config files before execution
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter is autonomous and can generate research outputs from external APIs, while oh-my-openagent exposes team_send_message and task creation tools. If oh-my-openagent treats dexter’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into messages or tasks without verification. The downstream action surface makes the blast radius larger than a simple hallucination.
conditions: IF dexter output is forwarded into team_send_message or task creation
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks dexter’s claims
mitigations: Require source links for every factual claim
Insert a verification checklist before messaging
Limit task creation to drafts only
Review one sample output before enabling automation
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before actions

E_compliance.rationale: dexter touches financial data and market data, while oh-my-openagent touches project code, session history, and provider authentication data. If those data classes are mixed in one workflow, retention and residency obligations can diverge across tools and APIs. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is routed through oh-my-openagent logs or telemetry
IF either agent retains shared session history beyond the intended retention window
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared sessions
Disable telemetry for sensitive runs
Document retention settings for both tools
Purge session history after each run
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
